claims.statement: TFM App assembles shared app services and per-window WindowModel workspace and UI state; TFI App retains app services and a registry of native scene-session workspace owners, while MobileSceneModel holds per-scene navigation and presentation.

Platform-local Application directories hold use-case and injectable service state rather than native UI or schema implementations; architecture tests reject forbidden imports in both, concrete implementation tokens in desktop Application and both apps' Features, and enforce SwiftData models and repository declarations in shared Persistence.

The desktop MCP application directory implements external tool and transfer operations, whereas desktop Infrastructure separates loopback HTTP transport, MCP protocol/session handling, and token storage.

Desktop Database contains adapters over Persistence-owned entities rather than a second schema; mobile Infrastructure stores connection-intent descriptors, excludes credentials and live state, and preserves unreadable snapshots.

AI feature directories provide conversation components while Assistant directories compose navigation; Shell directories define app navigation rather than remote execution, and desktop Terminal versus mobile Workspaces implement native runtimes whose mobile collection is owned in App/MobileWorkspaceSessionModel.

Native UI helpers separate reusable interaction from resource-specific operations: desktop managed cards receive selection/reordering capabilities, while mobile DesignSystem computes safe continuous or split content regions without becoming a session owner.

Vault composes specialized native resource-management surfaces, including mobile connection History, while Settings assembles independently owned settings capabilities and SFTP browser presentation remains separate from process-level transfer coordination.

Platform folders implement native OS integrations, including desktop window/menu-bar/file and audio services and mobile background, Live Activity, document, camera and terminal services; app resource groups retain platform-specific icons.

Native app composition adapts platform device naming into the shared device directory: TFM uses the trimmed kern.hostname with DeviceKit fallback and refreshes on application activation; TFI uses DeviceKit's Device.current.safeDescription and refreshes on active scene transitions.

The desktop app creates one shared AppModel and SwiftData container while its WindowGroup constructs a separate WindowModel per window; the AppDelegate handles native application activation, reopen, and termination, including confirmation of outstanding SFTP edits.

MCPServerController owns server configuration and lifecycle, binds loopback HTTP streaming requests to application upload/download coordinators and protocol requests to MCPServerProtocol, and stops transfers when the server stops or its token rotates.

MCPUploadCoordinator validates run-bound upload tickets and incoming PUT authorization, origin, headers, length and acknowledged resume offset before allocating capacity; interrupted or recoverable failures can pause for offset-based retry, while integrity failures or cancellations cannot, and successful state follows remote transfer completion.

MobileRootView retains scene navigation and reports phase, removal and Pro changes to app-wide MobileAppModel; MobileWorkspaceSessionModel publishes a restored workspace before connecting so repeated selection within its native window reuses the same runtime, whereas another window has an independent session.

MobileAppModel.reconcileSync starts five coordinators (Vault, connection History, Device, Metrics and Settings) only with an active tracked scene and Pro vault-sync eligibility, otherwise pauses all five; in-memory composition omits live cloud coordinators.

When all registered mobile scenes first become backgrounded, MobileAppModel pauses app-wide services and begins a UIKit background-task lease without immediately disconnecting healthy workspaces; expiration suspends sessions, forwarding, transfers and Assistant work, and active reentry finishes the lease and resumes affected workspaces and services.

MobileBackgroundController owns an at-most-once UIKit background-task lease: it ignores stale expiration callbacks, retires a returned identifier even if expiration occurred synchronously during begin, and does not end an invalid task.

MobileAppModel.setSyncEnabled checks Pro before enabling, persists the preference, routes History selection through its per-kind coordinator policy, migrates custom passwords when the iCloud master is enabled, then reconciles app-level sync.

MobileFeatureRegistry registers top-level destinations and MobileRootView mounts each in a NavigationStack backed by a scene-local MobileSceneModel; the Vault registration passes scene callbacks for opening/activating hosts, executing snippets, switching to Metrics and presenting a host editor.

Mobile Vault renders grouped host cards and resource links; tapping a host selects or opens a preferred terminal workspace through the scene, explicit SSH/Telnet/SFTP menu actions open connections, and local edit/group/deletion presentation does not own the app's session or host-deletion lifecycle.

Mobile Vault search forwards matching resource queries to dedicated pushed screens and switches the top-level destination for Metrics results; History presentation lives in the Vault file but filters host/device-backed app connection events through Application/Workspaces policy, caps results at 50 and only opens enabled protocols, with delete/clear operations delegated to app.connectionHistory.

MobileHostEditor holds host and custom-identity drafts in a sheet, gates save on protocol/port/authentication/environment validation and saves identity changes through the host library; the separate Known Hosts screen edits validated trust entries via app.knownHosts and reports storage failures.

Desktop RootView mounts one WindowSidebarView alongside persistent detail per WindowModel; the sidebar selects Navigator, compact Assistant, Snippets or focus-sensitive History, whose source depends on the focused SSH/SFTP pane and is disabled for serial/Telnet panes with a Snippets fallback; activating Assistant or Navigator can also change top-level destination.

Desktop Settings navigation belongs to each WindowModel: opening Settings remembers the previous destination, back traverses parent routes, and closing resets the route and restores the destination or falls back to Vault if its workspace disappeared; SettingsPageView renders the selected route within RootView's detail overlay.

Desktop Settings assembles category forms over app-owned settings and services rather than owning MCP or sync lifetimes; remote MCP editor presentation is Pro-gated, and the local MCP server has a separate Settings route.

When leaving a desktop Settings editor or Settings itself, empty provider, invalid new MCP server and blank new skill drafts are discarded; configured provider and substantive skill drafts survive, while a new MCP server must lock its namespace or be removed.

Desktop app composition creates shared app state and a per-window model; a failed local container initialization aborts startup, while AppDelegate defers quit to recheck pending SFTP edits, cancel on refusal, or save window size and await cleanup with a one-time three-second termination reply.
RootView keeps workspace content mounted in a persistent deck beneath non-workspace destinations, so switching to Vault, Assistant, Metrics or Settings hides but does not destroy session views.

Mobile startup presents a data-store failure screen instead of mounting MobileRootView if MobileAppModel composition throws, whereas desktop startup fatally aborts on failed local container or app composition.

On mobile restoration, saved workspace descriptors with missing hosts are pruned or closed; a workspace store read or write failure is surfaced as app error, and a failed read fences writes rather than replacing unreadable saved data.
Desktop app delegate can launch hidden at login and controls reopening of windows independently of a Settings route.

When mobile scene selection opens a workspace from another destination, MobileSceneModel defers selecting its ID until Workspaces activates, then focuses its Live Activity; a missing workspace instead clears selection and presents an unavailable alert.

Desktop Vault page, manager selection and editor route are window-local; VaultWorkspaceView retains the manager list while presenting work detail, and its dirty editor transition allows save, discard or cancel without proceeding after a failed save.

Mobile connection History leaves events for now-disabled host protocols visible but disallows opening them; search matches host, login, protocol or source-device name, and the Vault History surface limits the result to 50.

Closing a desktop workspace disconnects its connections and pushes it onto a ten-entry reopening stack; closing the window disconnects all workspaces and clears that stack instead of preserving their sessions.

Each mobile native scene's persistent UIKit session ID binds to a MobileWorkspaceSessionModel that owns its live workspaces, saved descriptors and display order; connection creation, close, rename, batch startup and snippet execution operate on that receiving scene's session rather than an app-global workspace deck.

The mobile workspace store saves one versioned device-local snapshot of per-session connection-intent descriptors and legacy unassigned descriptors; cold-launch first binding consolidates existing records into one scene in a single save without connecting them, and failed binding fences another scene from claiming the same records.

Mobile scene disconnect or view disappearance does not discard its persistent workspace session; UIKit explicit discard removes that session's descriptors and closes its workspaces without closing other windows, including workspaces previously handed off from the discarded window.

Only when UIKit's open-session reconciliation identifies an orphaned owner does the mobile app hand its live workspaces and descriptors to an active native session; it saves new ownership before transferring objects and keeps the original owner on save failure, avoiding a new connection or history event.

Mobile activity links route by workspace UUID to the owning persistent native scene via UIKit activation instead of creating a duplicate runtime in the receiving scene; failed activation reports unavailable.

MobileAppModel aggregates workspaces across all native session owners for scene-wide background expiration, host-deletion cleanup, connection history and Live Activity updates, while MobileWorkspaceSessionModel owns the connection and descriptor mutations for an individual window.
